findings.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the cache-status query
findings.body: The delete-cache mutation only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback. Unlike the credential deletion mutation below it, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. Since `onSuccess` is optional and is not contractually required to refetch this query, the component can continue displaying the old `cacheUpdatedAt` and the delete action after the server has removed all cache rows. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` on settlement/success of this mutation (and optionally retain the caller callback).

findings.title: Expired cache rows are reported as active cache status
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups every `CalendarCache` row for the credential, without restricting results to rows whose `expiresAt` is still in the future. Cache reads explicitly reject expired rows, but this status endpoint will continue returning their `updatedAt`, so the UI reports cache data as present and offers deletion even when there is no usable cached availability. Filter the status query by `expiresAt >= now` (or otherwise clearly represent expired cache separately).

findings.title: The new authorization and deletion behavior has no automated coverage
findings.body: There are no tests for the newly introduced destructive tRPC handler or the cache-status enrichment. This leaves unverified that a user can delete only cache rows belonging to their own credential, that an unauthorized credential ID is rejected without deleting rows, and that cache status selects the newest timestamp per credential. Add handler/repository tests for these cases before relying on this endpoint from the UI.
